claim: The white-footed deermouse Peromyscus leucopus is a key reservoir in North America for agents of several zoonoses, including Lyme disease, babesiosis, anaplasmosis, and a viral encephalitis.
source: The white-footed deermouse Peromyscus leucopus , a long-lived rodent, is a key reservoir in North America for agents of several zoonoses, including Lyme disease, babesiosis, anaplasmosis, and a viral encephalitis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Peromyscus leucopus remains persistently infected without apparent disability or diminished fitness.
source: While persistently infected, this deermouse is without apparent disability or diminished fitness.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior studies (Schwanz et al., 2011; Voordouw et al., 2015).

claim: Deermice were distinguished from mice and rats by LPS response profiles consistent with non-classical monocytes and alternatively-activated macrophages.
source: Deermice were distinguished from the mice and rats by LPS response profiles consistent with non-classical monocytes and alternatively-activated macrophages.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by RNA-seq data and gene expression analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: LPS-treated P. leucopus displayed little transcription of interferon-gamma in contrast to mice and rats.
source: LPS-treated P. leucopus , in contrast to mice and rats, also displayed little transcription of interferon-gamma and lower magnitude fold-changes in type 1 interferon-stimulated genes.
evidence: This finding is supported by targeted RNA-seq data and genome-wide expression analysis presented in the results.

claim: LPS-treated P. leucopus displayed lower magnitude fold-changes in type 1 interferon-stimulated genes compared to mice and rats.
source: LPS-treated P. leucopus , in contrast to mice and rats, also displayed little transcription of interferon-gamma and lower magnitude fold-changes in type 1 interferon-stimulated genes.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing fold-changes for ISGs like Mx2, Ifit1, Irf7, Isg15, and Oas1a.

claim: The phenomenon of reduced interferon response in P. leucopus was associated with comparatively reduced transcription of endogenous retrovirus sequences.
source: The phenomenon was associated with comparatively reduced transcription of endogenous retrovirus sequences and cytoplasmic pattern recognition receptors in the deermice.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq analysis of ERV sequences and comparison with mice and rats.

claim: The phenomenon of reduced interferon response in P. leucopus was associated with comparatively reduced transcription of cytoplasmic pattern recognition receptors.
source: The phenomenon was associated with comparatively reduced transcription of endogenous retrovirus sequences and cytoplasmic pattern recognition receptors in the deermice.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing reduced expression of Rigi, Ifih1, Dhx58, and Cgas in deermice.

claim: P. leucopus has a two-to-three fold longer life span than the house mouse, Mus musculus.
source: A related question—conceivably with the same answer—is what accounts for the two-to-three fold longer life span for P. leucopus than for the house mouse, Mus musculus (Labinskyy et al., 2009; Sacher and Hart, 1978)?
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies on longevity.

claim: Most deermice remain persistently infected with tickborne pathogens but display scant inflammation in affected tissues.
source: Most deermice remain persistently infected but display scant inflammation in affected tissues (Cook and Barbour, 2015; Long et al., 2019; Moody et al., 1994), and without apparent consequence for fitness (Schwanz et al., 2011; Voordouw et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Peromyscus species are more closely related to hamsters and voles in family Cricetidae than to mice and rats of family Muridae.
source: Peromyscus species, including the hantavirus reservoir P. maniculatus (Morzunov et al., 1998), are more closely related to hamsters and voles in family Cricetidae than to mice and rats of family Muridae (Bradley et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a phylogenetic study.

claim: Within 2 hr of LPS treatment, animals of both P. leucopus and M. musculus displayed piloerection and sickness behavior.
source: Within 2 hr LPS-treated animals of both species displayed piloerection and sickness behavior, that is reduced activity, hunched posture, and huddling.
evidence: This is an observational finding from the experimental protocol.

claim: By 4 hr after LPS treatment, 8 of 10 M. musculus had tachypnea, while only one of ten LPS-treated P. leucopus displayed this sign.
source: By the experiment's termination at 4 hr, 8 of 10 M. musculus treated with LPS had tachypnea, while only one of ten LPS-treated P. leucopus displayed this sign of the sepsis state (p=0.005).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiment with statistical significance.

claim: Deermice had lower mean hematocrit at 42% compared to M. musculus at 56%.
source: But overall the deermice had lower mean (95% confidence interval) hematocrit at 42 (36-48)%, hemoglobin concentration at 13.8 g/dL (12.1–15.5), and mean corpuscular volume for erythrocytes at 49 fL (47-51) than M. musculus with respective values of 56 (51-62)%, 16.1 g/dL (14.6–17.7), and 60 fL (58-62) (p<0.01).
evidence: This is supported by hematology data from the experiment.

claim: The mean numbers of white blood cells in the LPS groups in both species were lower than those of control groups.
source: In contrast to red blood cells, the mean numbers of white blood cells in the LPS groups in both species were lower than those of control groups (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by hematology data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Among LPS-treated animals, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio was 0.18 for mice and 0.64 for deermice.
source: But under the LPS condition. the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio was 0.18 (0.11–0.28) for mice and 0.64 (0.42–0.97) for deermice (p=0.0006).
evidence: This is supported by hematology data with statistical significance.

claim: Control group mice and deermice and LPS-treated mice had similar percentages (~5%) of monocytes in their blood.
source: Control group mice and deermice and LPS-treated mice had similar percentages (~5%) of monocytes in their blood; the mean monocyte percentage rose to 10% in LPS treated deermice (p=0.12).
evidence: This is supported by hematology data from the experiment.

claim: The mean monocyte percentage rose to 10% in LPS treated deermice.
source: Control group mice and deermice and LPS-treated mice had similar percentages (~5%) of monocytes in their blood; the mean monocyte percentage rose to 10% in LPS treated deermice (p=0.12).
evidence: This is supported by hematology data from the experiment.

claim: Eosinophil percentages tended to be higher in deermice at a mean 3.4% than mice at 1.2% under either condition.
source: Eosinophil percentages tended to be higher in deermice at a mean 3.4 (2.1–4.7)% than mice at 1.2 (0.5–1.9)% under either condition (p=0.004).
evidence: This is supported by hematology data with statistical significance.

claim: Principle component analyses revealed that untreated controls had coherent profiles within each species.
source: Principle component analyses (PCA) of the P. leucopus data and M. musculus data revealed that untreated controls had coherent profiles within each species (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: LPS-treated M. musculus were in a tight PCA cluster with the exception of one mouse.
source: With the exception of one mouse, the LPS-treated M. musculus were also in a tight PCA cluster.
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: LPS-treated deermice displayed a diversity of genome-wide transcription profiles and limited clustering.
source: In contrast, the LPS-treated deermice displayed a diversity of genome-wide transcription profiles and limited clustering.
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: For both species, the number of genes with higher expression with LPS exposure exceeded those with lower or unchanged expression.
source: For both species, the number of genes with higher expression with LPS exposure exceeded those with lower or unchanged expression.
evidence: This is supported by genome-wide RNA-seq analysis.

claim: The up-regulated gene profile for P. leucopus featured terms associated with 'neutrophil degranulation', 'myeloid leukocyte activation', 'leukocyte migration', and 'response to molecule of bacterial origin'.
source: The up-regulated gene profile for P. leucopus featured terms associated with 'neutrophil degranulation', 'myeloid leukocyte activation', 'leukocyte migration', and 'response to molecule of bacterial origin'.
evidence: This is supported by GO term analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Distinctive GO terms for up-regulated genes distinguishing mice from deermice were 'response to virus', 'response to interferon-beta', 'response to interferon-gamma', 'response to protozoan', and 'type II interferon signaling'.
source: Distinctive GO terms for up-regulated genes distinguishing mice from deermice were 'response to virus', 'response to interferon-beta', 'response to interferon-gamma', 'response to protozoan', and 'type II interferon signaling'.
evidence: This is supported by GO term analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Among the top 100 mouse DEGs, 20 were constituents of GO terms 'response to virus' or 'response to interferon-beta'.
source: Among the 100 mouse DEGs, 20 were constituents of GO terms 'response to virus' or 'response to interferon-beta' and only hree were members of GO term sets 'response to molecule of bacterial origin' or 'response to lipopolysaccharide'.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of top DEGs.

claim: Among the top 100 deermouse DEGs, only 2 were associated with the virus or type 1 interferon GO terms, but 12 were associated with bacterial molecule GO terms.
source: In contrast, among the top 100 deermouse DEGs, there were only 2 associated with the virus or type 1 interferon GO terms, but 12 were associated with either or both of the bacterial molecule GO terms.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of top DEGs.

claim: For mice, the Ifng transcript was one of the top ranked DEGs by both fold-change and adjusted p value by genome-wide RNA-seq.
source: For mice the Ifng transcript was one of the top ranked DEGs by both fold-change and adjusted p value by genome-wide RNA-seq (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by genome-wide RNA-seq data.

claim: For P. leucopus, Il1b was the comparably ranked DEG instead of Ifng.
source: In contrast, for P. leucopus Ifng was far down the list, and the comparably ranked DEG instead was Il1b.
evidence: This is supported by genome-wide RNA-seq data.

claim: There was little or no detectable transcription of Ifng in the blood of deermice in which Il1b expression was high.
source: There was little or no detectable transcription of Ifng in the blood of deermice in which Il1b expression was high.
evidence: This is supported by targeted RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 8.

claim: Both groups of LPS-treated rats had elevations of interferon-gamma, interleukin-6, and interleukin-10 proteins from undetectable levels in the blood.
source: There were also elevations of interferon-gamma, interleukin-6, and interleukin-10 proteins from undetectable levels in the blood of the treated rats.
evidence: This is supported by multiplex cytokine assay data from the rat experiment.

claim: By targeted RNA-seq, there were 24 x fold-changes between the LPS-treated rats and control rats for Ifng and Nos2 but only ~3 x fold-change for Il1b.
source: By targeted RNA-seq, there were 24 x fold-changes between the LPS-treated rats and control rats for Ifng and Nos2 but only ~3 x fold-change for Il1b (Table 4).
evidence: This is supported by targeted RNA-seq data from the rat experiment.

claim: Interferon-gamma is a determinant of Nos2 expression.
source: Interferon-gamma is a determinant of Nos2 expression (Lowenstein et al., 1993; Salkowski et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: There was a tight correlation between the levels of transcription of Ifng and Nos2 for both species and both experimental conditions.
source: The analysis shown in upper left panel of Figure 10 shows a tight correlation between the levels of transcription of Ifng and Nos2 for both species and both experimental conditions (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 10.

claim: Five ISGs (Gbp4, Ifit1, Irf7, Isg15, and Oas1a) had higher transcription in all the LPS-treated animals but the magnitude of fold change was less in the deermice, ranging from 6–25% of what it was in the LPS group of mice.
source: Five other ISGs (and encoding genes)—guanylate binding protein 4 (Gbp4), interferon-induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeat (Ifit1), interferon regulatory factor 7 (Irf7), ubiquitin-type modifier ISG15 (Isg15), and 2'–5' oligoadenylate synthase 1 A (Oas1a)—had higher transcription in all the LPS-treated animals. But the magnitude of fold change was less in the deermice, ranging from 6–25% of what it was in the LPS group of mice (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by targeted RNA-seq data.

claim: All four cytoplasmic PRRs (Rigi, Ifih1, Dhx58, and Cgas) were upregulated in the blood of LPS-treated mice and deermice, but the magnitude of fold change was less by 50–90% in treated P. leucopus than in M. musculus.
source: All four cytoplasmic PRRs were upregulated in the blood of LPS-treated mice and deermice (Supplementary file 1). But, again, for each of them the magnitude of fold change was less by 50–90% in treated P. leucopus than in M. musculus.
evidence: This is supported by targeted RNA-seq data.

claim: Two of the three highest scoring DEGs in rats by FDR p value and fold-change criteria were a gag-pol transcript for an ERV polyprotein and an env transcript for an envelope protein similar to that of murine leukemia viruses.
source: Two of the three highest scoring DEGs by FDR p value and fold-change criteria were a gag-pol transcript (GenBank accession XM_039101019.1) for an ERV polyprotein and an env transcript (XM_039113367) for an envelope (Env) protein that is similar to that of murine leukemia viruses (MLV) (Table 4; Table 4—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by genome-wide RNA-seq data from the rat experiment.

claim: There were four MLV-type or other ERV env transcripts among the 1266 genome-wide RNA-seq DEGs for M. musculus.
source: There were four MLV-type or other ERV env transcripts among the 1266 genome-wide RNA-seq DEGs for M. musculus.
evidence: This is supported by genome-wide RNA-seq data.

claim: There was no transcripts for an ERV Env protein annotated as such among the 1154 DEGs identified for P. leucopus.
source: But, there was no transcripts for an ERV Env protein annotated as such among the 1154 DEGs identified for P. leucopus (Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: This is supported by genome-wide RNA-seq data.

claim: In P. leucopus, transcription of the env sequence was lower in LPS-treated animals than in controls.
source: In contrast, in P. leucopus the magnitudes of fold-change upwards for gag-pol was less than in mice or rats, and transcription of the env sequence was actually lower in LPS-treated animals than in controls.
evidence: This is supported by targeted RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 12.

claim: Similarities in the profiles for the LPS-treated and B. hermsii-infected deermice included low levels of transcription of Nos2 and Ifng that contrasted with the high levels for Arg1 and Il1b expression.
source: Similarities in the profiles for the LPS-treated and B. hermsii-infected deermice were as follows: (1) low levels of transcription of Nos2 and Ifng that contrasted with the high levels for Arg1 and Il1b expression in the same animals
evidence: This is supported by targeted RNA-seq analysis of B. hermsii-infected deermice.

claim: The responses that distinguish deermice are not confined to the singular case of LPS as the elicitor.
source: Thus, the responses that distinguish deermice are not confined to the singular case of LPS as the elicitor.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of LPS and B. hermsii infection experiments.

claim: LPS stimulated expression of ERV sequences in mice or mouse cells.
source: The results confirm previous reports of heightened transcription of ERV sequences in mice or mouse cells after exposure to LPS (Hara et al., 1981; Jongstra and Moroni, 1981; Stoye and Moroni, 1983).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies and confirmed by data in this study.

claim: A second, indirect effect of LPS on the mouse is through its provocation of increased ERV transcription intracellularly.
source: It follows that a second, indirect of LPS on the mouse is through its provocation of increased ERV transcription intracellularly.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of ERV upregulation following LPS treatment.

claim: ERV-origin RNA, cDNA and/or protein would be recognized by a cytoplasmic PRR.
source: ERV-origin RNA, cDNA and/or protein would then be recognized by a cytoplasmic PRR.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between ERV expression and PRR signaling.

claim: RIG-I was one PRR associated with ERV transcription in this study.
source: RIG-I was one associated with ERV transcription in this study.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis between Rigi and ERV expression.

claim: Intracellular PRR signaling can trigger a type 1 interferon response.
source: As was demonstrated for LINE type retrotransposons in human fibroblasts, intracellular PRR signaling can trigger a type 1 interferon response (De Cecco et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: There was heightened transcription of retrotransposons in patients with septic shock.
source: In humans, there was heightened transcription of retrotransposons in patients with septic shock (Mommert et al., 2020), as well as in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from human subjects experimentally injected with LPS (Pisano et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Bacteria like Staphylococcus epidermidis that express TLR2 agonists promoted expression of ERVs, which in turn modulated host immune responses.
source: Bacteria like Staphylococcus epidermidis that express TLR2 agonists, such as lipoteichoic acid, promoted expression of ERVs, which in turn modulated host immune responses (Lima-Junior et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: A synthetic analog of a B. burgdorferi lipoprotein activated human monocytic cells and promoted replication of the latent HIV virus in cells that were persistently infected.
source: A synthetic analog of a B. burgdorferi lipoprotein activated human monocytic cells and promoted replication of the latent HIV virus in cells that were persistently infected (Norgard et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: The suppression of ERV expression in deermice may be attributable to defensive adaptations of Peromyscus to repeated invasions of endogenous retroviruses.
source: This suppression in the deermice may be attributable to defensive adaptations of Peromyscus to repeated invasions of endogenous retroviruses, as Gozashti et al. has proposed for P. maniculatus (Gozashti et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on citation to a prior study.

claim: P. leucopus has an abundance of Long Terminal Repeat retrotransposons, several named for their endogenous retrovirus heritages.
source: Like P. maniculatus, P. leucopus has an abundance of Long Terminal Repeat retrotransposons, several named for their endogenous retrovirus heritages (Long et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior genomic study.

claim: Nos2 gene knockouts in M. musculus had lower LPS-induced mortality than their wild-type counterparts.
source: Although Nos2 gene knockouts in M. musculus had lower LPS-induced mortality than their wild-type counterparts, the mutants were more susceptible to the protozoan Leishmania major and the facultative intracellular bacterium Listeria monocytogenes (MacMicking et al., 1995; Wei et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Nos2 gene knockout mice were more susceptible to Leishmania major and Listeria monocytogenes.
source: Although Nos2 gene knockouts in M. musculus had lower LPS-induced mortality than their wild-type counterparts, the mutants were more susceptible to the protozoan Leishmania major and the facultative intracellular bacterium Listeria monocytogenes (MacMicking et al., 1995; Wei et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: P. yucatanicus is the main reservoir for Leishmania mexicana in Mexico.
source: While there are no known studies of either of these pathogens in P. leucopus, the related species P. yucatanicus is the main reservoir for Leishmania mexicana in Mexico (Chable-Santos et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Compared with M. musculus, which suffer a high fatality rate from experimental infections with L. mexicana, P. yucatanicus infections are commonly asymptomatic.
source: Compared with M. musculus, which suffer a high fatality rate from experimental infections with L. mexicana, P. yucatanicus infections are commonly asymptomatic (Loría-Cervera et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Both tolerance of and resistance to the tickborne encephalitis flavivirus Powassan virus by P. leucopus were demonstrated in an experimental model in which mice were severely affected.
source: Both tolerance of and resistance to the tickborne encephalitis flavivirus Powassan virus by P. leucopus were demonstrated in an experimental model in which mice, by contrast, were severely affected Mlera et al., 2017.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: P. maniculatus has been successfully infected with the SARS-CoV-2 virus by the respiratory route, but the infected animals displayed only mild pathology, manifested little if any disability, and recovered within a few days.
source: P. maniculatus has been successfully infected with the SARS-CoV-2 virus by the respiratory route, but the infected animals displayed only mild pathology, manifested little if any disability, and recovered within a few days Fagre et al., 2021; Griffin et al., 2021.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Among natural populations and in the laboratory, P. maniculatus is noted for its tolerance of hantavirus, which commonly is fatal for infected humans.
source: Among natural populations and in the laboratory, P. maniculatus is noted for its tolerance of hantavirus, which commonly is fatal for infected humans Botten et al., 2000; Childs et al., 1994.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: P. maniculatus was permissive of infection with monkeypox virus, but the infection was mild and transient.
source: P. maniculatus was permissive of infection with monkeypox virus, but the infection was mild and transient Deschambault et al., 2023.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Naked mole-rat macrophages and blood myeloid cells have low to absent transcription of Nos2 or production of nitric oxide in response to LPS, even in the presence of added interferon-gamma.
source: These include macrophages and blood myeloid cells with low to absent transcription of Nos2 or production of nitric oxide in response to LPS, even in the presence of added interferon-gamma Gorshkova et al., 2023.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Like P. leucopus and in distinction to M. musculus, naked mole-rats showed an increase in the proportion of neutrophils in the blood 4 hr after intraperitoneal injection of LPS.
source: Like P. leucopus and in distinction to M. musculus, naked mole-rats showed an increase in the proportion of neutrophils in the blood 4 hr after intraperitoneal injection of LPS Hilton et al., 2019.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: The hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells of naked mole-rats had a lower type 1 interferon response than mice to a TLR3 agonist.
source: In another comparative study, the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells of these rodents had a lower type 1 interferon response than mice to a TLR3 agonist Emmrich et al., 2022.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: A natural population of P. leucopus had >80% prevalence of infection and high incidence of re-infections by B. burgdorferi.
source: Our studies of P. leucopus began with a natural population and documented a>80% prevalence of infection and high incidence of re-infections by B. burgdorferi in the area's white-footed deermouse, the most abundant mammal there (Bunikis et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior field study.

claim: Most humans who become infected with B. burgdorferi have a definable illness.
source: Subclinical infections in humans occur, but most of those who become infected have a definable illness (Steere et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior clinical study.

claim: The majority of the symptoms and signs of Lyme disease are attributable to inflammation elicited by the organism's presence and not from virulence properties per se or the hijacking of host cells.
source: The localized or systemic presence of the microbe is a necessary condition for Lyme disease, but the majority of the symptoms and signs are attributable to inflammation elicited by the organism's presence and not from virulence properties per se or the hijacking of host cells (Coburn et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior review and represents established knowledge.

claim: Humans are transmission dead-ends for B. burgdorferi and many other zoonotic agents in their life cycles.
source: Since humans are transmission dead-ends for B. burgdorferi and many other zoonotic agents in their life cycles, it is not surprising that human infections are generally more debilitating if not fatal than what adapted natural hosts experience.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of zoonotic disease ecology.

claim: CD14 is required for LPS-stimulated signaling through surface TLR4.
source: CD14 is required for LPS-stimulated signaling through surface TLR4 Mazgaeen and Gurung, 2020, and, as such, its decreased availability for this signaling pathway is a possible explanation for the moderated response to LPS in P. leucopus.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Decreased availability of CD14 for TLR4 signaling is a possible explanation for the moderated response to LPS in P. leucopus.
source: CD14 is required for LPS-stimulated signaling through surface TLR4 Mazgaeen and Gurung, 2020, and, as such, its decreased availability for this signaling pathway is a possible explanation for the moderated response to LPS in P. leucopus.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observed decrease in CD14 expression.

claim: The response to LPS by P. leucopus is consistent with the alternatively-activated or M2 type macrophage polarization, rather than the expected classical or M1 type.
source: By the criteria summarized above, the response to LPS by P. leucopus is consistent with the alternatively-activated or M2 type, rather than the expected classical or M1 type.
evidence: This is supported by multiple gene expression ratios (Nos2/Arg1, Il12/Il10, Akt1/Akt2, Cd14/Fcgr3).

claim: The blood of untreated P. leucopus animals displayed M2 type polarization features.
source: But it was not only LPS-treated deermice that had this attribute, the blood of untreated animals also displayed M2 type polarization features.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data from control animals.

claim: A xenotropic MLV-related retrovirus has been discounted as a cause of chronic fatigue syndrome.
source: A xenotropic MLV-related retrovirus has been discounted as a cause of chronic fatigue syndrome (McClure and Kaye, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Production of whole virions need not occur for there to be PRR signaling in response to cytoplasmic Env protein, single stranded RNA, or cDNA.
source: However, production of whole virions need not occur for there to be PRR signaling in response to cytoplasmic Env protein, single stranded RNA, or cDNA (Russ and Iordanskiy, 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: The 20 P. leucopus in the combined experiment were of a mean 158 days of age and had a mean 21 g body mass.
source: For the combined P. leucopus-M. musculus experiment, the 20 P. leucopus were of a mean (95% confidence interval) 158 (156-159) days of age and had a mean 21 (19-22) g body mass.
evidence: This is descriptive data about the experimental animals.

claim: The 20 M. musculus in the combined experiment were all 149 days of age and had a mean body mass of 47 g.
source: The 20 M. musculus were all 149 days of age and had a mean body mass of 47 (43-50) g.
evidence: This is descriptive data about the experimental animals.

claim: Animals were intraperitoneally injected with either E. coli O111:B4 LPS at a dose of 10 µg per g body mass or sterile saline.
source: At 15 min intervals and alternating between species, sex, and treatments, animals were intraperitoneally (ip) injected 50 µl volumes of either ion-exchange chromatography-purified Escherichia coli O111:B4 LPS (Sigma-Aldrich L3024) in a dose of 10 µg per g body mass or the diluent alone: sterile-filtered, endotoxin-tested, 0.9% sodium chloride (Sigma-Aldrich).
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol.

claim: Animals were euthanized at 4.0 hr after injection.
source: At 4.0 hr time after injection animals were euthanized as described above, and sterile dissection was carried out immediately.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol.

claim: In the lower dose experiment, P. leucopus were administered LPS at 1.0 µg/g and euthanized 12 hr after injection.
source: In an experiment with six P. leucopus, the animals were administered the same single dose of LPS but at 1.0 µg/g and the same control solution. The animals were euthanized 12 hr after the injection the following day.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol for the lower dose experiment.

claim: For the P. leucopus and M. musculus samples, production of cDNA libraries was with the Illumina TruSeq Stranded mRNA kit.
source: For the P. leucopus and M. musculus samples production of cDNA libraries was with the Illumina TruSeq Stranded mRNA kit.
evidence: This describes the methods used for RNA-seq.

claim: The libraries were sequenced on a Illumina NovaSeq 6000 instrument with paired-end chemistry and 150 cycles to achieve ~100 million reads per sample.
source: After normalization and multiplexing, the libraries were sequenced at the University of California Irvine's Genomic High Throughput Facility on a Illumina NovaSeq 6000 instrument with paired-end chemistry and 150 cycles to achieve ~100 million reads per sample for the combined P. leucopus-M. musculus experiment.
evidence: This describes the sequencing methods.

claim: For P. leucopus of the combined experiment, a mean of 83% of the reads mapped to the genome transcript reference set of 54,466.
source: For P. leucopus of this experiment, a mean of 83% of the reads mapped to the genome transcript reference set of 54,466; mean coverages for all transcripts and for the mean 62% of reference transcripts with ≥1 x coverage were 97 x and 157 x, respectively.
evidence: This describes the RNA-seq mapping results.

claim: For M. musculus of the combined experiment, a mean 91% of the reads mapped to the genome transcript reference set of 130,329.
source: For M. musculus of this experiment, a mean 91% of the reads mapped to the genome transcript reference set of 130,329; mean coverages for all transcripts and for the mean of 21% of reference transcripts with ≥1 x coverage were 103 x and 568 x, respectively.
evidence: This describes the RNA-seq mapping results.
